channel.title: Pendle Council Transparency — AI DOGE
channel.description: Independent analysis of Pendle Borough Council spending and governance.

item.title: Fuelmate: 5,047 Fuel Fill-Ups and the Fleet Size Question
item.description: Pendle made 5,047 individual fuel card transactions through Fuelmate Ltd (£800K, £159 average). That's ~4.5 fills per working day over 4.5 years. Does Pendle's fleet actually justify this volume, or are personal vehicles being fuelled on the council's tab?

item.title: Orchard Recycling: 304 Payments Every 7.6 Days Like Clockwork
item.description: Orchard Recycling Service received £661K across 304 payments at 7.6-day intervals. Risk score: 40/100 (elevated) with no Companies House registration. Clock-like regularity in a single department suggests automated payments without transaction-level oversight.

item.title: Liberata: Why Does Burnley Pay 2.2x More for the Same Outsourcer?
item.description: Pendle pays Liberata UK £16.7M. Burnley pays £36.7M — 2.2x more for the same Bain Capital-owned outsourcer. Burnley insourced 4 services in April 2025. Should Pendle do the same? What's the actual contract scope difference?

item.title: 777 Split Payment Instances: £19.5M Below the Radar
item.description: 777 instances of payments to the same supplier within short windows that individually fall below approval thresholds. £19.5M suspected. Vehicle hire patterns inflate the count, but even discounting fleet payments, the volume is the highest of any election council.

item.title: 49,741 Transactions on £125M: Why Pendle Processes More Than Anyone
item.description: Pendle has the highest transaction volume of any Lancashire election council despite the lowest total spend. Go Plant Fleet (210+ identical £3,540 charges), Fuelmate (5,047 fill-ups), and Riverside Truck Rental (133+ identical charges) drive the volume. Is per-unit invoicing efficient or wasteful?

item.title: 23 Suppliers With Companies House Breaches: The Most in Lancashire
item.description: Pendle has 23 suppliers with current Companies House compliance issues — the highest count of any Lancashire council. £815K spent with companies in breach of filing requirements.

item.title: PEARL JV: Public Money, Undeclared Conflicts, and the Barnfield Connection
item.description: PEARL is Pendle's version of Burnley's Barnfield JV. Grant Thornton auditors warned in January 2025 that directors 'do not always declare conflicts of interest'. The Barnfield empire spans 5 councils totalling £38.8M.

item.title: 1,682 Payments to 'Redact - Personal Data': Every 7.2 Days for £870K
item.description: Pendle paid £870.9K to a supplier recorded only as 'Redact - Personal Data' — 1,682 payments at 7.2-day intervals. The same pattern appears at Preston (£1.01M). Combined: £1.88M in hidden spending.
